headline: NEGATIVE: the dual-route fix via a SINGLE shared pool + whole-form->affix cross-route INHIBITION does NOT achieve rule generalization. Across inhib-strength 0.5..6.0 (7 points, seed 42) reg_acc caps at 0.25 (needs 0.90) while blocking holds (irr 0.86-1.0); 0 points pass BOTH gates. reg_acc is ~the single-pool baseline (0.19) REGARDLESS of inhibition -> the single-pool+inhibition realization does NOT truly separate the routes: novel stems still spuriously activate whole-forms in the shared WTA, so the default affix never wins. Blocking works (inhibition suppresses the affix for irregulars), the RULE does not. Next: GENUINELY separate pools (route 1 in a dedicated pool isolated from the whole-form store), the true Pinker-Ullman separation; + the Dale-compliant di-synaptic interneuron for the inhibition.
